question: Should memory-core dreaming accept user-selectable localized journal/report labels now, and should the accepted contract be a bounded `dreaming.language` key, a custom template/prompt override, or no localization surface yet?
rationale: The request is useful but adds public plugin config and localization policy surface; repository policy sets a high bar for new config/default surfaces and the cluster already has overlapping open PRs.

options.title: Review one language-key implementation
options.body: Use the linked implementation candidate as the landing path only if maintainers accept a bounded `dreaming.language` contract and require schema, docs, tests, and real output proof before merge.

options.title: Consolidate under the older tracker
options.body: Retarget this issue and the linked PRs to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/79223 if maintainers want a broader language/prompt design before accepting code.

options.title: Decline localization for now
options.body: Keep English structural labels until OpenClaw has a broader localization strategy or stronger product demand for memory-core output localization.

recommendation.title: Review one language-key implementation
recommendation.body: Use the linked implementation candidate as the landing path only if maintainers accept a bounded `dreaming.language` contract and require schema, docs, tests, and real output proof before merge.
